subject: maths
title: Year 2 Halves, Quarters and Eighths
seo_title: Year 2 Fractions Worksheets: Halves, Quarters and Eighths (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise and describe one-half as one of 2 equal parts of a whole and connect halves, quarters and eighths through repeated halving
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on halves, quarters and eighths for the Australian Curriculum: equal parts, one half, one quarter and one eighth of shapes, pizzas and sandwiches, repeated halving, half and quarter of a collection, and everyday problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: One half is one of 2 equal parts. Halve a half to get a quarter. Halve a quarter to get an eighth.
key_sub: The parts must be equal. More parts means smaller parts, so one eighth is smaller than one quarter.
body_html:
Equal parts

A fraction is a part of a whole. The parts must be equal (the same size).

One half is one of 2 equal parts.

Equal partsEach part isWe write
2one half12
4one quarter14
8one eighth18

Halve, then halve again

Cut a half in half and you get quarters. Cut a quarter in half and you get eighths.

So 2 quarters make one half, and 2 eighths make one quarter.

More parts means smaller parts. One eighth is smaller than one quarter.

Half and quarter of a collection

To find one half of a group, share it into 2 equal groups. Count one group.

Example

What is one quarter of 8?

Share 8 into 4 equal groups: 2, 2, 2 and 2. One group is 2.

Answer: 2

Example

What is one quarter of 20?

Halve 20 to get 10. Halve 10 to get 5.

Answer: 5

Example

How many minutes are in half an hour?

An hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30.

Answer: 30 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 2 unequal parts “halves”Halves must be equal
Thinking 18 is bigger than 14 because 8 is biggerMore parts means smaller parts
Saying half of 12 is 22 is the number of groups. Count one group: 6
Counting the parts that are not shadedCount the shaded part, then all the equal parts

faq.q: What fractions do Year 2 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 2 (AC9M2N03) students recognise one half as one of 2 equal parts of a whole. They connect halves, quarters and eighths by halving again and again.

faq.q: Why is one eighth smaller than one quarter?
faq.a: A whole cut into 8 equal parts has smaller parts than the same whole cut into 4. Each quarter is cut in half to make 2 eighths.

faq.q: How do you find a quarter of a number?
faq.a: Halve the number, then halve it again. For a quarter of 12, half of 12 is 6 and half of 6 is 3, so the answer is 3.
No. NAPLAN starts in Year 3. Halves, quarters and eighths in Year 2 build the fraction skills used in Year 3.

items.q: Which shape is cut into halves?
items.e: Halves are 2 equal parts. That is B. A has 2 parts, but they are not equal. C has 4 equal parts. D has 2 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is cut into quarters?
items.e: Quarters are 4 equal parts. That is A. B has 4 parts, but they are not equal. C has 8 equal parts. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into eighths?
items.e: Eighths are 8 equal parts. That is C. A has 4 equal parts. B has 8 parts, but they are not equal. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is not cut into equal parts?
items.e: Look for parts that are different sizes. That is D. A has 4 equal parts. B has 2 equal parts. C has 8 equal parts.

items.q: What are the parts called?
items.e: There are 2 equal parts. 2 equal parts are called halves.

items.q: Halves are how many equal parts?
items.e: 2 equal parts make halves. Each part is one half.

items.q: Quarters are how many equal parts?
items.e: 4 equal parts make quarters. Each part is one quarter.

items.q: Eighths are how many equal parts?

items.q: Leo cuts his toast into 2 pieces. One piece is big. One piece is small. Are the pieces halves?
items.e: Halves must be 2 equal parts. One piece is bigger, so they are not halves.

items.e: The shape has 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. So 12 is shaded (one half).

items.q: What fraction is shaded?
items.e: The shape has 4 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. So 14 is shaded (one quarter).

items.e: The pizza has 8 equal pieces. 1 piece is eaten. So 18 of the pizza is eaten (one eighth).

items.q: 1 piece of the pizza is eaten. What fraction of the pizza is eaten?
items.e: The pizza has 4 equal pieces. 1 piece is eaten. So 14 of the pizza is eaten (one quarter).

items.q: 1 piece of the pizza is eaten. What fraction of the pizza is eaten?
items.e: The pizza has 2 equal pieces. 1 piece is eaten. So 12 of the pizza is eaten (one half).

items.q: Which shape has one half shaded?
items.e: One half is 1 of 2 equal parts. That is B. A has 2 parts, but they are not equal. C shows one quarter. D has 2 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape has one quarter shaded?
items.e: One quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts. That is D. A shows one eighth. B shows one half. C has 4 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape has one eighth shaded?
items.e: One eighth is 1 of 8 equal parts. That is B. A shows one quarter. C has 8 parts, but they are not equal. D shows one half.

items.q: What do we call 1 of 4 equal parts?
items.e: 4 equal parts are quarters. One part is one quarter, written 14.

items.q: What do we call 1 of 8 equal parts?
items.e: 8 equal parts are eighths. One part is one eighth, written 18.

items.q: How do we write one half?
items.e: One half is 1 part out of 2 equal parts. The 1 goes on top and the 2 goes underneath: 12.

sets.title: Halving again: halves, quarters and eighths

items.q: Fold a paper strip in half. How many equal parts are there?
items.e: One fold makes 2 equal parts: 2 halves.

items.q: Fold a paper strip in half, then in half again. How many equal parts are there?
items.e: Each half is folded in half. 2 halves become 4 equal parts: 4 quarters.

items.q: Fold a paper strip in half 3 times. How many equal parts are there?
items.e: The parts double each time: 2, then 4, then 8. That is 8 eighths.

items.q: What is half of one half?
items.e: Cut a half into 2 equal parts. Each part is one quarter, 14.

items.q: What is half of one quarter?
items.e: Cut a quarter into 2 equal parts. Each part is one eighth, 18.

items.q: How many quarters make one half?
items.e: Halve a half and you get 2 quarters. So 2 quarters make one half.

items.q: How many eighths make one quarter?
items.e: Halve a quarter and you get 2 eighths. So 2 eighths make one quarter.

items.q: How many eighths make one half?
items.e: One half is 2 quarters, and each quarter is 2 eighths. 2 + 2 = 4 eighths.

items.q: How many quarters make one whole?
items.e: A whole cut into quarters has 4 equal parts. 4 quarters make 1 whole.

items.q: How many eighths make one whole?
items.e: A whole cut into eighths has 8 equal parts. 8 eighths make 1 whole.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is bigger?
items.e: Look at the bars: one quarter is longer than one eighth. Cutting into more parts makes smaller parts. So 14 is bigger.

items.q: Two cakes are the same size. Which is bigger: 12 of a cake or 14 of a cake?
items.e: Cut a cake into 2 and the pieces are big. Cut it into 4 and the pieces are smaller. So 12 is bigger.

items.q: The wholes are the same size. Which part is the smallest?
items.e: The more equal parts, the smaller each part. 8 parts is the most, so one eighth is the smallest.

items.q: The wholes are the same size. Which part is the biggest?
items.e: Only 2 equal parts, so each part is big. One half is bigger than a quarter or an eighth.

items.q: Kai says 18 is bigger than 14, because 8 is bigger than 4. Is he right?
c: No, 14 is bigger
items.e: Cutting into 8 parts makes smaller parts than cutting into 4. So 14 is bigger than 18.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Look at the shaded parts.
items.e: The shading stops at the same place. One half is the same as 2 quarters.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Look at the shaded parts.
items.e: The shading stops at the same place. One quarter is the same as 2 eighths.

items.q: 4 eighths are shaded. Which fraction is the same?
items.e: 4 of the 8 equal parts are shaded. That is half of the shape, so 4 eighths = one half.

items.q: 2 eighths are shaded. Which fraction is the same?
items.e: 2 eighths fill one quarter of the circle. So 2 eighths = one quarter.

items.q: Cut a square in half. Cut each part in half. Then cut each part in half again. What is each part called?
items.e: 2 parts, then 4 parts, then 8 equal parts. Each part is one eighth.

sets.title: Half and quarter of a collection

items.q: There are 6 apples in 2 equal groups. What is one half of 6?
items.e: Share 6 into 2 equal groups: 6 ÷ 2 = 3. One group is one half.

items.q: There are 10 apples in 2 equal groups. What is one half of 10?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups: 10 ÷ 2 = 5. One group is one half.

items.q: There are 14 apples in 2 equal groups. What is one half of 14?
items.e: Share 14 into 2 equal groups: 14 ÷ 2 = 7. One group is one half.

items.q: There are 8 apples in 4 equal groups. What is one quarter of 8?
items.e: Share 8 into 4 equal groups: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. One group is one quarter.

items.q: There are 12 apples in 4 equal groups. What is one quarter of 12?
items.e: Share 12 into 4 equal groups: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. One group is one quarter.

items.q: There are 20 apples in 4 equal groups. What is one quarter of 20?
items.e: Share 20 into 4 equal groups: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. One group is one quarter.

items.q: There are 16 apples in 8 equal groups. What is one eighth of 16?
items.e: Share 16 into 8 equal groups: 16 ÷ 8 = 2. One group is one eighth.

items.q: What is one half of these apples?
items.e: There are 12 apples. Share 12 into 2 equal groups: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. One group is one half.

items.q: What is one half of these apples?
items.e: There are 16 apples. Share 16 into 2 equal groups: 16 ÷ 2 = 8. One group is one half.

items.q: What is one quarter of these apples?
items.e: There are 8 apples. Share 8 into 4 equal groups: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. One group is one quarter.

items.q: What is one quarter of these apples?
items.e: There are 16 apples. Share 16 into 4 equal groups: 16 ÷ 4 = 4. One group is one quarter.

items.q: What is one half of these apples?
items.e: There are 20 apples. Share 20 into 2 equal groups: 20 ÷ 2 = 10. One group is one half.

items.q: What is one half of 40?
items.e: Share 40 into 2 equal groups: 40 ÷ 2 = 20. One group is one half.

items.q: What is one half of 60?
items.e: Share 60 into 2 equal groups: 60 ÷ 2 = 30. One group is one half.

items.q: What is one half of 100?
items.e: Share 100 into 2 equal groups: 100 ÷ 2 = 50. One group is one half.

items.q: What is one quarter of 40?
items.e: Share 40 into 4 equal groups: 40 ÷ 4 = 10. One group is one quarter.

items.q: Half of 12 is 6. Half of 6 is 3. What is one quarter of 12?
items.e: A quarter is half of a half. Halve 12 to get 6, then halve 6 to get 3.

items.q: Find one quarter of 24. Halve it, then halve it again.
items.e: Half of 24 is 12. Half of 12 is 6. So one quarter of 24 is 6.

items.q: Find one eighth of 24. Halve it 3 times.
items.e: Half of 24 is 12. Half of 12 is 6. Half of 6 is 3. So one eighth of 24 is 3.

items.q: Half of a number is 7. What is the number?
items.e: 7 is one half. The whole is 2 halves: 7 + 7 = 14. Check: half of 14 is 7.

items.q: What time does the clock show?
items.e: The long hand points to 6. It has gone half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is just past 3. It is half past 3.

items.q: What time does the clock show?
items.e: The long hand points to 3. It has gone one quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is just past 9. It is quarter past 9.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30: 30 + 30 = 60.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30, and half of 30 is 15. So a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Oliver eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza does he eat?
items.e: 4 equal slices are quarters. Oliver eats 1 slice: one quarter, 14.

items.q: Aarav cuts an orange into 8 equal pieces. He eats 1 piece. What fraction of the orange does he eat?
items.e: 8 equal pieces are eighths. 1 piece is one eighth, 18.

items.q: Mum cuts a sandwich in half. Then she cuts each half in half again. How many equal pieces are there?
items.e: Each of the 2 halves becomes 2 pieces: 2 + 2 = 4 pieces. Each piece is one quarter.

items.q: Two pizzas are the same size. Ava eats 14 of one pizza. Jack eats 18 of the other pizza. Who eats more?
items.e: A pizza cut into 4 has bigger slices than a pizza cut into 8. 14 is bigger than 18, so Ava eats more.

items.q: Zara cuts a pizza into 2 pieces. One piece is much bigger. She says her piece is one half. Is she right?
c: No, the pieces are not equal
items.e: Halves must be 2 equal parts. One piece is bigger, so the pieces are not halves.

items.q: There are 24 students in a Year 2 class. Half of them walk to school. How many students walk?
items.e: Share 24 into 2 equal groups: 24 ÷ 2 = 12 students. One group is one half.

items.q: Mia has 20c. She spends half of it at the school canteen. How much does she spend?
items.e: Half of 20c: share 20c into 2 equal parts. 10c + 10c = 20c, so the answer is 10c.

items.q: A carton has 12 eggs. One quarter of the eggs are brown. How many eggs are brown?
items.e: Share 12 into 4 equal groups: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 eggs. One group is one quarter.

items.q: Mei has $10. She gives half of it to her sister. How much does she give?
items.e: Half of $10: $5 + $5 = $10. So the answer is $5.

items.q: Ethan sees 16 kangaroos in a paddock. Half of them are eating grass. How many kangaroos are eating grass?
items.e: Share 16 into 2 equal groups: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 kangaroos. One group is one half.

items.q: Kai has a ribbon 20 cm long. He cuts it in half. How long is each piece?
items.e: Share 20 cm into 2 equal parts: 10 cm + 10 cm = 20 cm. Each piece is 10 cm.

items.q: An orange is cut into 8 equal pieces. Sienna eats 2 pieces. What fraction of the orange is that?
items.e: 2 eighths make one quarter, because halving a quarter gives 2 eighths. So Sienna eats one quarter.

items.q: Noah has 18 stickers. Half of them are koalas. How many koala stickers does he have?
items.e: Share 18 into 2 equal groups: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 stickers. One group is one half.

items.q: A cake is cut into 4 equal pieces. One quarter of the cake is eaten. How many quarters are left?
items.e: The cake has 4 quarters. 1 is eaten: 4 − 1 = 3 quarters are left.

items.q: Charlotte has 20 grapes. She eats one quarter of them. How many grapes are left?
items.e: Half of 20 is 10. Half of 10 is 5. So one quarter of 20 is 5. Charlotte eats 5 grapes. 20 − 5 = 15 grapes are left.

items.q: Grace finds some shells at the beach. Half of them are white. 9 shells are white. How many shells does she find?
items.e: 9 shells are one half. The whole is 2 halves: 9 + 9 = 18 shells. Check: half of 18 is 9.
